Counsel for Opposite Party :- Archana Singh,G.A.
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
1. None appeared on behalf of the High Court Legal Services Committee even in revised call.

2. Heard Shri Ram Jatan Yadav, learned counsel for the applicant and Shri Suresh Bahadur Singh,
learned A.G.A. for the State-respondent.

3. The instant bail cancellation application has been filed seeking cancellation of the bail granting order of opposite party no.4 dated 04.10.2023 passed by Additional Sessions Judge/Special Judge (POCSO Act-I), Hathras in Case Crime No.381 of 2023, under Sections 376(B,D) IPC & Sections 5m/6 POCSO Act, 2012, Police Station Sadabad, District Hathras, during pendency of the trial in the court below.

entities.text: Additional Sessions Judge/Special Judge (POCSO Act-I), Hathras
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
4. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that applicant is the informant of the case and he has filed the instant bail cancellation application on the ground that age of the victim was hardly twelve years and she in her statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. stated that opposite party no.4 committed rape upon her alongwith two others but inspite of that court concerned granted bail to him and therefore, court concerned committed grave illegality in granting the bail to opposite party no.4 and considering the age of the victim and her statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C.
bail granted to opposite party no.4 is liable to be cancelled.

sentences.text:
5. Learned A.G.A. also submits that victim is a minor girl aged about twelve years and she in her statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. stated that applicant and two others committed rape upon her but could not dispute the fact that victim in her statement recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C. did not even disclose the name of the applicant and there are material contradictions in both the statements of the victim recorded during investigation.
6. I have heard learned counsel for both the parties and perused the record of the case.
7. This is the bail cancellation application filed by the applicant on the ground that court concerned wrongly granted bail to opposite party no.4 as victim is a minor girl aged about twelve years and she in her statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. categorically stated that applicant and two others committed rape upon her but from the bail granting order passed by the court concerned, it reflects that in her statement recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C., victim did not even disclose the name of the applicant and from perusal of both the statements of the victim, it reflects that there is major contradiction in both the statements of the victim.
8. Further, law is settled that it is easy to reject a bail application but it is very difficult to cancel a bail already granted and for cancellation of bail, very cogent and overwhelming reasons are necessary, which in my considered view is missing in the present matter.
9.
Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case, discussed above, in my view, the instant bail cancellation application is devoid of merit and is accordingly dismissed.

Order Date :- 12.11.2024/Zafar  Jay Kishor vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/36320477/
